Amazon.com (NASDAQ:AMZN), the global e-commerce, logistics, and cloud computing platform, closed at $257.75, down 3.34%. Tech weakness and AI-chip concerns pressured shares, along with a setback in its bid to build a satellite network. A deal selling a majority stake in several data centers added to investor uncertainty.
Trading volume reached 47.3 million shares, coming in nearly 2% above its three-month average of 39.4 million shares. Amazon.com IPO'd in 1997 and has grown 263,133% since going public.

How the markets moved today

The S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC) fell 1.92% to 7,416, and the Nasdaq Composite (NASDAQINDEX:^IXIC) declined 2.49% to 24,510. Among broadline retail and e-commerce peers, Walmart closed at $128.41, up 0.25%, while Target ended at $160.32, down 0.70%, as investors also tracked holiday demand estimates.

What this means for investors

Amazon shares moved on several news items today. A new U.S. rule tightening access to advanced AI chips in parts of Asia and Brazil has pressured AI infrastructure companies, including Amazon.

Company-specific news also disappointed Amazon investors today. A United Launch Alliance Vulcan rocket failed in flight minutes after launching from Florida, and the 40 Amazon internet satellites it carried never reached orbit. The malfunction during Sunday's climb is a major blow to ULA's new heavy-lift rocket and a costly disruption to both companies' launch schedules. The satellites were to be part of Amazon's Leo low-Earth-orbit satellite broadband network.

Amazon Web Services also announced a $5 billion data center deal with Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust. Selling a majority stake in some of its data center infrastructure may also have added to investor concerns about the AI sector.

title: Is There A Risk Hiding In Walmart Stock's Latest Quarter?
detail:
Is There A Risk Hiding In Walmart Stock's Latest Quarter?
Trefis Team

WMT
AMZN
COST
TGT
KR
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Image from Pixabay

For questions about this article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com.

Walmart (WMT) has received nearly $2.9 billion in tariff refunds, a sum equal to about 9% of its operating income over the twelve months to July 2026. Only part of that reached profit, because Walmart is spending some of it on lower prices. The refunds gave the retailer's profit a lift in its fiscal second quarter, and management expects their effect to be largely contained within fiscal 2027. So how much of Walmart's recent profit growth came from the refunds?

How Much Did The Refunds Add To Walmart's Profit?

During its August 20, 2026 call, management said the refunds provided a net benefit of about 750 basis points to operating income growth in fiscal Q2 2027, the quarter that ended July 31. That figure accounts for the money Walmart reinvested in lower prices. Adjusted operating income grew 17.4% in constant currency. Without the refunds, management said, growth landed at the top end of its 7% to 10% guidance.

The company's reported figures, which are not adjusted, also rose. Walmart said its gross profit rate rose 96 basis points in the quarter, mainly because of the tariff refunds. Its reported operating margin reached 5.0%, against 4.1% in the same quarter a year earlier.

Walmart Expects Slower Profit Growth After The Refunds

Management expects operating income to grow only 2% to 4% in constant currency in fiscal Q3 2027, the three months to October, and that guide includes the refund money it plans to spend on prices. Adjusted earnings per share grew over 19% in fiscal Q2 2027, the quarter with the refunds. Management also said that matching that 19% earnings per share growth will be a challenge in fiscal 2028.

This slowdown matters because of what holders are paying. Walmart shares trade at 46.2 times its trailing earnings, compared with 21.9 for the S&P 500, and those twelve months include the refund quarter. A multiple that high needs profit to keep growing faster than sales once the refunds are spent, which management has said it expects.

What Supports Walmart's Profit Beyond The Refunds?

Walmart's newer businesses are the best evidence against the worry. Global advertising grew 38% in fiscal Q2 2027. Management said operating income grew 10% excluding the tariff refunds, and that almost half of that growth came from areas like membership, advertising and marketplace. Membership income grew nearly 17% across the company, and management expects the share of growth from these businesses to continue.

title: Target vs. Walmart Stock:  Which is the Better Buy Ahead of Q3 Earnings?
detail:
Target vs. Walmart Stock: Which is the Better Buy Ahead of Q3 Earnings?
Shaun Pruitt
Mon, November 16, 2026 at 12:50 PM CST 3 min read
TGT
WMT
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Retail giants Target TGT) and Walmart WMT) are preparing to report their much-anticipated Q3 results this week, with Wall Street looking for insight into consumer spending trends ahead of the critical holiday shopping season.

With inflation and affordability concerns still influencing purchasing decisions, investors will be particularly focused on comparable-store sales, e-commerce growth, and demand for discretionary merchandise versus everyday essentials.

That said, let's compare Target and Walmart's Q3 expectations, stock performance, valuations, and dividends to determine which may be the better investment.

Target & Walmart Q3 Expectations

Target reports Wednesday, November 18, before the opening bell. The Zacks Consensus Estimate calls for Q3 earnings of $2.04 per share, representing nearly 15% year-over-year growth, on revenue of $26.41 billion, up more than 4%.

Walmart reports Thursday, November 19, before the market opens. The Zacks Consensus Estimate calls for Q3 earnings of $0.64 per share, up 3% YoY, on revenue of $186.52 billion, a nearly 4% increase.

Walmart's competitive pricing, grocery dominance, and expanding e-commerce operations remain key growth drivers, while Target is benefiting from improving profitability and efforts to strengthen discretionary sales.

Both retailers' holiday outlooks will be particularly important as consumers balance spending on necessities and nonessential purchases.

Stock Performance & Valuation Comparison

Target has significantly outperformed Walmart in 2026, posting a year-to-date total return of 70% compared with Walmart's 16%.

However, Walmart has delivered stronger long-term performance, generating a three-year total return of +155%, noticeably outpacing Target's 39%, the Zacks Retail-Wholesale sector's 57%, and the benchmark S&P 500's 80%.

Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Still, Target has a far more attractive valuation, trading at 17X forward earnings compared with the Zacks Retail-Wholesale sector average of 22X and Walmart's 40X.

Target's substantial discount may appeal to value-oriented investors, although Walmart's consistent sales growth, defensive business model, and expanding digital capabilities help justify its premium.

Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

TGT & WMT Dividend Comparison

Both retailers have impressive dividend histories, although Target offers substantially higher income.

Target pays a quarterly dividend of $1.16 per share, translating to an annual payout of $4.64 and a yield near 3%. Walmart pays $0.2475 quarterly, equating to $0.99 annually and a yield of roughly 0.8%.

Gross margin more than doubled to 23.9% through a combination of operational streamlining, increased sales volume offsetting fixed costs, and a transition from direct store delivery to retailer distribution centers.

The 'Farm to Formula' strategy is designed to diversify revenue by leveraging established retail relationships to enter higher-value food, beverage, and nutrition categories.

A commercial supply agreement with Kandy Fork Farms aims to improve scalability by transitioning selected growing activities to a partner, avoiding the need for internal infrastructure expansion.

Management attributes the 14% revenue growth to expanded programs with major retailers like Walmart, Kroger, and Target, particularly within the cut herb portfolio.

Operational efficiency was highlighted by a 4% decline in cost of goods sold despite an increase in total sales volume, reflecting improved throughput and financial discipline.

The company is positioning itself as a 'change agent' in private label, moving away from simple knockoffs toward innovative, nutrient-dense products that drive retailer market share.

Infrastructure Development and Product Launch Timelines

The transition of production activities to Kandy Fork Farms is expected to begin in Q4 2026 and be substantially completed during 2027, targeting a production cost decline of more than 12%.

The Prairie Hills manufacturing platform is being developed with an annual capacity exceeding 100 million beverage units to support protein, sports nutrition, and functional wellness categories.

Management plans to launch new plant-based product innovations, developed in collaboration with Square Roots, at Expo West in March.

The company intends to initially utilize co-manufacturing partners for new beverage awards before transitioning volume into the internal Prairie Hills facility to optimize margins.

Future growth is predicated on a dual-track approach: strengthening core produce profitability while scaling the addressable market through the Farm to Formula initiative.

Key Structural and Commercial Developments

Completed the $6.3 million acquisition of the Prairie Hills property in October 2026, transitioning from tenant to owner using Series B preferred stock and a 5-year secured note.

Secured a major private label ready-to-drink protein beverage award from a global grocery retailer operating more than 2,000 stores.

Appointed a senior project manager from Tetra Pak to lead the development of the Prairie Hills manufacturing platform and aseptic packaging initiatives.

Became the primary herb supplier at UNFI's Mid-Atlantic distribution center, providing access to an additional 1,500 retail locations.

Target (TGT), the leading general merchandise retailer competing with Walmart (WMT) and Costco (COST), is working to regain its growth momentum after a prolonged period of declining sales and softer discretionary demand.

The company is now undertaking a significant business overhaul, with a sharper focus on merchandise, convenience, and operational efficiency. Since Michael Fiddelke became CEO in February, the retailer has been refining its product assortment, improving the shopping experience, and strengthening its competitive position.

Faster order fulfillment is another vital part of this transformation. Target is investing heavily in same-day and next-day services to keep pace with changing online shopping habits, and its Q2 FY2026 results suggest that these efforts are gaining traction.

The next important update is scheduled for Wednesday, Nov. 18, when Target releases its Q3 FY2026 financial results before the market opens. The numbers and management commentary would offer a better understanding of how the turnaround is progressing and what lies ahead for the retail giant.

About Target Stock

Target offers an extensive merchandise selection spanning clothing, beauty, groceries, electronics, home furnishings, household essentials, toys, and pet supplies. With a market cap of nearly $73.4 billion, the Minneapolis, Minnesota-based retailer serves customers through its physical stores and digital platforms, including Target.com.

TGT stock has also delivered an impressive performance over the past year, gaining 78% in the last 52 weeks. Its year-to-date (YTD) advance stands at 64%, while shares have climbed 32% over the past six months, extending their upward momentum.

Its dividend history is another notable feature, with 58 consecutive years of dividend increases. The retailer currently pays an annual dividend of $4.64 per share, yielding 2.87%.
